description: Create a form and its empty first draft in a workspace this user may create in. The id is made from the slug and never changes. The form's title is authored in the builder afterwards; creating it changes nothing a respondent can reach.

Apply the draft you proposed with propose_draft to this form's working draft, for the user to review as a diff and confirm. Call propose_draft first. It publishes nothing and puts nothing live: the draft is stored as a draft and marked as changed by the assistant.

Save a complete draft to a form, through the same save path every edit in the builder takes. It publishes nothing and puts nothing live: the draft is stored as a draft and marked as changed by the assistant. This is how a form goes from blank to a reviewable draft, after form.create and any question.create steps of the same plan.

Publish the form's working draft to one environment: freeze it as the next version and make that version live there, in one act. Needs Edit forms and Publish forms for that environment. Where a non-production environment exists a draft is never published straight to production. The workflow and second approval apply exactly as they do on the screen.

Publish an existing version to one environment, including an earlier one, which makes that earlier version live again. Nothing is frozen. Production accepts only a version already live in a non-production environment, where one exists. The workflow revision, the destination's current state and second approval are all rechecked at confirmation, so a stale review is refused and writes nothing, exactly as on the screen.
Change the form's abuse-control settings. It affects sessions started from now on and leaves every session already under way untouched.
Close the form to new sessions in the current environment. Every session already under way keeps its pinned version and finishes normally.
Reopen the form to new sessions in the current environment.

Create one-time or reusable respondent links for a form, in the environment the person's screen is set to. You do not choose that environment and cannot name another one. A link reaches the form only where that form is already live, so read the form first and say which environment the links are for before they confirm. expiresAt must be an instant still to come: one already past is refused when they confirm. The turn's context gives you the instant the person's own clock is at and the zone it is read in, so work every expiry out from those rather than asking them how long it should last. Where they want to see what a lapsed link does, propose one a few minutes ahead and say when it lapses. The card shows that instant in their own zone rather than as you wrote it. The URLs are shown to the user once and are never returned to you.
Revoke one respondent link in the current environment.
Erase one respondent's answers and submission, recording a tombstone. It cannot be undone, and the user retypes the session id on the card before it can run.
Send one flagged response's withheld submission event on, so its consumers receive it.
Open the export dialog with these filters. The user presses Export and the file downloads in their browser; no part of it is returned to you.
Configure a new delivery endpoint for this form in the current environment. Its signing secret is shown to the user once and is never returned to you.
Replace an endpoint's signing secret. Deliveries signed with the old one stop verifying, and the new secret is shown to the user once.
Point an endpoint at another URL. The card names the endpoint and shows the new target in full, query string included.
Put a deactivated endpoint back in service in the current environment.
Stop delivering to an endpoint. The row and its delivery history stay, and a delivery already in flight keeps its own retry state.
Reset one dead-lettered delivery to due-now, so the worker attempts it again. It reads no part of the payload.
Create an access group in a workspace. The group grants nobody anything until somebody holds it, so creating one changes no access by itself.
Remove an access group and every grant it carried. Each holder loses that access at once, and one revoke row is written for each.

Grant an access group to one person, by address. Nothing offered to you reads the people on this site, so you cannot tell beforehand whether an address has an account: propose the address they gave you, and where there is no active account for it the step is refused at their Confirm and the card carries the reason. A self-grant of a response role is held for another administrator to approve while the workspace has second approval on.
Revoke one person from an access group. Everybody else in it keeps theirs.
Make a member an owner of the workspace, or take ownership away. Removing the last owner is refused.
Change the workspace's Second approval switch: whether a publish to production and a response self-grant need a second account.

Create a question and its first draft version in the library. The id is made once and never changes. Nothing pins the question until a form's draft does, and nothing serves it until the version is published.
Replace a draft version's definition. A published or deprecated version is refused: published content is immutable, so changing one means opening a new version.
Freeze a draft version and make it pinnable. Its content can never change again, and a form's draft that pins it stops reporting an unpublished pin.
Block new pins on a published version. Every form already pinned to it is untouched and keeps serving it.
Open a new draft version, seeded from the latest one. Nothing published changes, and no form moves to it until a draft pins the new version.

Reads one website once and answers the colours, the heading face and the logo a theme could start from, saving nothing. You never supply the address: the person types it on the card, where it is shown in full, and nothing is fetched until they confirm. Propose this when they ask for the form to look like their own site. What it finds is shown to them in the appearance panel, and no part of that page is sent to you.

Keeps the look the appearance panel is showing as a workspace theme, under the name you give, so every form in that workspace can pick it. You name only the theme; the colours, face, corners and logo are the ones in front of the person. Propose it once they are happy with a look, and never as a way to change the form itself.
